setlist_extra.title: That's It For The Other One

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mountains of the Moon** (2 reviews): Band members switched one by one from acoustic to electric guitars during the segue into Dark Star; The acoustic-to-electric transition into Dark Star is singled out as especially nice [8][9]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer treats this version as the yardstick against which all other Dark Stars are measured [8]
- **That's It For The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer's highlight: the Cryptical Envelopment reprise reaches mystic territory with Jerry driving the band into the cosmos [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mountains of the Moon**: rare: 14 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd69-02-22.sbd.owen.7860.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 110 min; rated 4.49/5 by 35 [1]. Said about its sound: The cleaned-up version has no hiss beyond what comes with 36-year-old analog tape, and sounds treble-rich; Reviewer finds the sound a little bassy, though allows it could be their own ears; A cut at 2:48 in Death Don't Have No Mercy likely loses several minutes [1][14][15]
- **gd1969-02-22.sbd.vernon.5206.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 110 min; rated 4.22/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: Notes list left-channel dropouts, pops and glitches, some fixed or removed, plus a cut or splice in the source tape [2]
- **gd1969-02-22.sbd.miller.112691.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 114 min; rated 4.62/5 by 24 [3]

## Around the show

- At the set break Jerry announced they would tune up, chat among themselves and drink cokes [10]
- Reviewer sees the show as a warm-up for the following week's Fillmore run, though it stands on its own [6]
- Reviewer names it one of two essential shows, the other being Binghamton 77 [8]
- Reviewer calls the show a good prelude to the Fillmore shows that followed [12]
- Reviewer ranks this Dark Star alongside the 2/28 version as a favorite of the year [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-02-22.sbd.owen.7860.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by The Wizard; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer has known the show from tape, then a hissy soundboard CD, and now this cleaned-up version; The circulating tape clips the first verse of Dupree's Diamond Blues [1][14]
- **gd1969-02-22.sbd.vernon.5206.shnf**: transferred by Matt Vernon; source: SBD > MR > R > R > DAT > CDR [2]. Also: Seed disks for this transfer were provided by Paul B [2]
- **gd1969-02-22.sbd.miller.112691.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1969-02-22 Sat Dream Bowl, Vallejo, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1353151926474/grateful-dead-1969-02-22-sat-dream-bowl) [17]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1969-02-22 Sat Dream Bowl, Vallejo, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1353151926474/grateful-dead-1969-02-22-sat-dream-bowl) [18]
